scope: First-pass dependency and proof-location audit, with targeted checks. This is not a line-by-line independent validation of all analytic estimates.

findings.title: Arrow convention and local height consistency
findings.label: Height convention
findings.question: Does the two-in/two-out rule give the stated unit height increments, with consistent signs?
findings.evidence: The starter Lean code proves equivalence of the ice rule and two incoming arrows; equivalence with zero elementary height circulation; construction and uniqueness of four adjacent face heights with a chosen anchor; and periodic-column sector conservation.
findings.remaining: Global integration over a simply connected domain, the infinite planar law and torus winding periods remain outside these local proofs. No full paper theorem is certified by this check.

findings.title: Balanced plane law and zero-slope identification for c at least one
findings.label: prop:physical-plane
findings.question: Is uniqueness being inferred merely from zero expected slope?
findings.evidence: No. The manuscript includes a variational-domain and ergodic-component argument. DKLM arXiv:2603.06268v1, Theorem 2.2 and the paragraph following equation (6), explicitly identify the balanced limit and describe it as a unique free-energy minimizer for the stated range. Lammers-Tassy arXiv:2004.15025v1, Theorem 13.16, states the six-vertex strict-convexity condition c+ c- >= max(a+ a-, b+ b-), matching c >= 1 when a=b=1.
findings.remaining: Formalize the precise variational functional and the domain-reduction argument, or import fully proved versions. Checking the citation statement is not re-proving the external result.

findings.title: Conditional normalization does not supply Gaussian convergence
findings.label: Final use of DKLM Theorems 4.3 and 4.4
findings.question: Does the proof assume its desired GFF limit when identifying the variance?
findings.evidence: The final proof invokes normalization after the preceding sections establish a GFF limit with undetermined coefficient. DKLM Theorem 4.3 explicitly assumes a subsequential GFF limit; Theorem 4.4 computes the free-energy curvature. Both state c in [1,2]. The manuscript uses a separate stiffness/overlap argument for c<1.
findings.remaining: Preserve this dependency order in Lean. Theorem 4.3 cannot be used to establish Gaussianity, and its range cannot be extended below c=1 without another proof.

findings.title: The cited twisted scalar-product identity exists
findings.label: lem:scalar-product
findings.question: Is the determinant formula actually supplied by the cited source?
findings.evidence: KMST arXiv:hep-th/0406190v1, Proposition 3.1 and equations (3.8)-(3.9), give the derivative-over-Cauchy determinant formula for a twisted on-shell vector and generic off-shell variables. The manuscript explains its monodromy rescaling and compensating twist factor, then treats coincident columns separately.
findings.remaining: Independently verify every normalization, slot order, pole cancellation and analytic specialization. The original theorem's presence does not by itself verify those conversions or all root-of-unity specializations.

findings.title: Uniform Gaudin and mixed-measure bounds
findings.label: lem:gaudin-inverse
findings.question: Why do inverses stay bounded when the terminal Bethe roots become sparse?
findings.evidence: A proof is present. It separates contracting dense rows from finitely many edge indices, extracts a one-sided limiting equation, and uses a decaying maximum-principle argument. The mixed operator is undressed into a positive-measure equation. Thus this is not justified merely by finite nonsingularity or diagonal dominance.
findings.remaining: Verify uniform edge-index bounds and local mass; passage to the extracted equation including tails; existence of a nonzero limiting coordinate; and the weighted perturbation bounds, in each declared order of limits. State a lower-bound theorem separately from an invertibility theorem on infinite-dimensional spaces.

findings.title: Joint determinant tails and exchanges of infinite-volume limits
findings.label: lem:weighted-flags; lem:joint-determinant-tails; prop:word-kernel
findings.question: Are simultaneous root escapes controlled strongly enough to sum the finite-word expansion?
findings.evidence: The weighted-flags lemma is followed by a joint-minor estimate and a locally uniform word-kernel limit. The proof adapts separate flag bases for positive and negative minors, extracts quadrature weights, and claims an exponential majorant. The array limit is explicitly lim(d->0) limsup(B->infinity), rather than an asserted limit at every fixed d.
findings.remaining: Check residue codimensions, nested flag dimensions, uniform constants and all near-coincidence cancellations. Construct the majorizing measure and prove dominated convergence before using the resulting word kernels. Fixed-word estimates must not be used for unbounded word length.

findings.title: A common analytic radius at boundary rows
findings.label: lem:scalar-continuation
findings.question: Does finite invertibility near a swap point give a radius independent of lattice size?
findings.evidence: The manuscript provides a folded two-auxiliary block calculation, a geometric bound on its complementary block, quotient bounds, then a wordwise continuation and a countable fiber construction. The preceding harmonic-row-normalization lemma separately handles vacuum denominator zeros inside the strip.
findings.remaining: Prove the displayed finite folded-block identities, both left and right quotient bounds and their uniform constants. Verify passage from word-dependent norm bounds to one scalar continuation radius on a common full-measure set. Finite analyticity alone is insufficient.

findings.title: Covariance normalization below c=1
findings.label: lem:stiffness; lem:infrared; lem:overlap-asymptotic; lem:detector-packing
findings.question: Are the twist derivatives and determinant asymptotics justified before the limits?
findings.evidence: There are separate lower and upper bounds for the orbit mass. The stiffness uses fixed-filling finite derivatives; the upper bound uses the finite twist-overlap Taylor coefficient, then a finite-trace analysis and a sampled symbol. The text explicitly takes Taylor coefficients before either array limit and supplies the deferred overlap proof later in the section.
findings.remaining: Re-derive the finite second-derivative identities, uniform root jets, inverse-row estimates, end corrections and Fourier/sampling calculation. Verify that no derivative of a limiting free energy is substituted for the required limit of finite derivatives. This is a central unverified analytic dependency.

findings.title: Two-scale spectral convergence needs all zeros controlled
findings.label: prop:two-scale
findings.question: Could zeros between the two observed scales alter the rescaled energies?
findings.evidence: The manuscript addresses this explicitly with an exterior-dip bound, an all-zero exceptional-event bound, fixed annular windows and a zero-count truncation before sending the mesh to zero. It defines representative convergence rather than asserting a bounded embedding of the whole tensor completion.
findings.remaining: Verify the state-measure exceptional-event estimate, the zero-count truncation, discontinuity-free spectral cutoffs and strong convergence on representatives. Compact-open convergence of spectral functions alone does not imply the claimed energy limits.

findings.title: Gaussianity requires the nonvacuum collision lemma
findings.label: lem:collision; prop:gaussian-currents
findings.question: What establishes Wick's rule beyond two-point covariance?
findings.evidence: The collision lemma claims weak convergence of a damped two-current operator to -kappa times the identity, including nonvacuum exterior states. It uses another scale separation, contour formulas and uniform dyadic cutoff removal. The subsequent proposition removes artificial poles, rules out a simple collision residue, and derives Wick recursion.
findings.remaining: Prove the collision operator limit, its uniform norm majorant and the interchange with strongly converging exterior vectors. Verify joint holomorphy and moving-pole removal. This is the central Gaussianity obligation; knowing the variance is insufficient.

findings.title: Nonsmooth tests and negative function-space conventions
findings.label: lem:log-integrability; prop:finite-energy; prop:negative-regularity; prop:intrinsic-dual
findings.question: Do the smooth-test limit and logarithmic bounds imply every advertised topology?
findings.evidence: Separate proofs are supplied for finite-energy measures, restriction Besov/Hölder/Sobolev norms, the source's outward-scaling completion, and intrinsic Sobolev duals on arbitrary bounded open sets. The finite-energy proof includes the case where distinct continuum points round to the same lattice face. The intrinsic proof treats small-area cells by a thick/thin decomposition.
findings.remaining: Fix exact definitions of each negative Sobolev realization before formalization. Independently check logarithmic domination, mollification in energy, separability, compactness, pinning and thin-cell estimates. The phrase 'usual ... realization' needs an explicit definition; these spaces must not be silently identified on irregular domains.

findings.title: Endpoint rotation requires a loop bijection, not just close loop sets
findings.label: lem:rr-nails; thm:rr-rotation; prop:endpoint-completion
findings.question: Does the external FK rotation argument preserve multiplicity and endpoint separation information?
findings.evidence: The appendix deliberately uses the homotopy coupling before its metric conclusion. The cited rotation paper, arXiv:2012.11672v2, Definition 3.8 and Sections 3.5-3.6, does define homotopic similarity using a bijection of nontrivial loops and matching crossing words. Lis arXiv:2004.05337v2, Lemma 3.1, supplies the stated infinite-volume loop-law convergence at c=2. The OAI appendix includes fair-sign averaging, loop counts, point avoidance and a nail-window extraction.
findings.remaining: Verify the full extracted coupling with its exact marginals, parameter scales, orientations and multiplicities; the inside/outside transfer; and uniform integrability of the sign-averaged polynomial. The external set-distance rotation theorem alone would not prove this step. The complete extraction is not independently verified here.
